_meta.source: Real entries filtered from Caroma-Poc/journeyAX/data/cdl/template-library.json (sport === HOCKEY, case-insensitive match on 12 of 364 total catalog entries).
_meta.assetDownloadEvidence: All render/svg pairs below were downloaded live from service.augustasportswear.com (Scene7 image server) on 2026-08-27 and verified as real files (PNG via `file`, SVG via header inspection) — see assets/augusta-live/hockey/{sku}/. Three SKUs (228154, 228252, 228254) consistently returned HTTP 408 across multiple size-code retries and were confirmed to have NO real asset (matches their renderable:false catalog flag).
_meta.glbDeliveryFinding: Checked live on momentecbrands.com (Augusta/Momentec's real storefront, WebSphere Commerce). PDP for 228103 (https://www.momentecbrands.com/freestyle-performance-series-traditional-lace-up-hockey-jersey-cut-228103) uses ASGPDP_FullImage (a 2D pan/zoom image viewer) and ASGInspirationDesignView (a Scene7-based 2D customizer that composes color/text/mascot layers onto the flat PNG). Full network request log inspected: no .glb, .gltf, or any 3D-viewer asset request appeared anywhere. Verdict: NO real GLB/3D delivery exists on Augusta's live site today — 2D Scene7 image compositing only.
_meta.svgStructureFinding: The downloaded SVGs are NOT decorative mockups — they are real flat-pattern CUT-PIECE sheets (confirmed visually: distinct panel outlines for front body, back body, sleeves, collar, cuffs, gussets, lace strips, each sheet carries a 'PATTERN COLORS' swatch legend + '{sku}-{size}' label, e.g. '228103-L'). Group-ID naming is NOT fully consistent across styles: lace-up/V-neck styles (228103, 228108, 228203, 228208) use a flat 'outlines' group with no front/back/sleeve subdivision; reversible/V-neck-2.0 styles (228150, 228162, 228250, 228262) additionally carry an empty 'guides' group with placeholder front/back/sleeve zone markers (no geometry) used only for decoration placement, not real panels. One style (228108) has a typo'd group id 'oulines' vs 'outlines' elsewhere, and uses hyphenated 'text-front/back/sleeves' vs underscored 'text_front/back/sleeve' elsewhere -- real, unforced inconsistency, not a uniform schema.
_meta.uvVsCutPieceVerdict228103: PARTIAL MATCH. Real evidence: SVG 228103 visually decomposes into ~15 distinct real cut-piece panels (front body, back body, 2 sleeve panels, collar V-piece, 2 cuff/gusset pieces, a diamond gusset, 4 rectangular panels, a long lace strip). The local GLB (Caroma-Poc/3d-garment-retexture/models/228103.glb) has 4 sub-meshes with UV-connected-component island counts of 25/10/12/16; restricting to substantial islands (>400 verts, i.e. real panels not stitch/eyelet noise) the main shell mesh alone has ~10, same order of magnitude as the SVG's ~15. Largest UV islands (main torso front/back) have aspect ratios 1.21-1.23, broadly consistent with the SVG's roughly-square front/back torso panels. However: SVG groups/paths carry NO semantic labels (front/back/sleeve are NOT individually tagged inside 'outlines' -- confirmed by parsing, all children are anonymous <g>/<path> with no id), and the GLB carries extra mesh layers (a full separate liner mesh 228103_3, and a paired-eyelet mesh 228103_2) with no SVG counterpart. So: real structural correspondence in KIND and rough magnitude/proportion (both are genuine flat-panel decompositions of the same garment construction) but NOT a verified, automatable 1:1 geometric mapping -- a manual or algorithmic panel-matching step would still be required before this could feed bake/wrap automation.
